claims.claim: Phase/type erasure can remove a finite agreement-violation witness in an explicit certificate-driven locking schema.
claims.scope: Existential schema family; not a universal statement about all BFT protocols.

claims.claim: Closure-added actions preserve finite unsafety under a preorder with increasing insertions, forward simulation, transitivity, and upward-closed Unsafe.
claims.scope: Every protocol instantiation must supply and justify a meaningful preorder.

claims.claim: For every f≥1, n=3f+1 and q=2f+1 admit the stated quorum-pivot separation between G_T and both G_D edge choices.
claims.scope: Exact arithmetic and branch construction for the supplied schema.

claims.claim: The supplied seven-flag model is strict exactly under S2 ∧ D ∧ T ∧ E_d ∧ X ∧ (S1 ∨ R_q).
claims.scope: Exact only for the supplied seven-flag operational abstraction.

claims.claim: Exact replay is observationally erasable under stable-key idempotence and a state-based safety observation.
claims.scope: No timer, output, resource, voting-power, or future-behavior effect from duplicates.

claims.claim: Counting message instances rather than unique logical contributions creates a replay-only quorum counterexample.
claims.scope: Controlled defective accumulator; not an allegation about a client.

claims.claim: The constructive embeddings G_P⊆G_D⊆G_T⊆G_M⊆G_R and G_D⊆G_D1 hold in the artifact models.
claims.scope: No inclusion claimed between G_D1 and G_T.

claims.claim: Under G_T, admitting E while withholding R lets the pivot support both conflicting branches.
claims.scope: Depends on the controlled defective transition and no replacement contributor.

claims.claim: Under type-uniform G_D, edge-off leaves the first branch at q−1 and edge-on delivers repair before the second branch, leaving it at q−1.
claims.scope: Two branch choices in the defined closure model.

claims.claim: Exactly three of 128 premise assignments are strict: 0111111, 1101111, and 1111111.
claims.scope: Bit order is fixed by the artifact documentation.

claims.claim: Two independent bounded locking kernels reproduce the same zero/nonzero scheduler-detection classes for the selected controlled defects.
claims.scope: Bounded kernels, not production clients.

claims.claim: The fuller event loop is safe for the baseline under all three checked grammars and unsafe only for G_T under MISSING_LOCK_UPDATE.
claims.scope: Six controlled terminal cases.

claims.claim: The independent Go and Python fuller event-loop implementations agree on all six terminal cases.
claims.scope: Agreement covers the selected terminal signatures and safety classification.

claims.claim: FIFO, LIFO, and 256 seeded random queue orders preserve the classification across 1,548 case runs.
claims.scope: Robustness to the enumerated event-order policies, not arbitrary unbounded scheduling.

claims.claim: Five positive SMT/CHC files yield eight expected UNSAT outcomes.
claims.scope: Solver-checked encodings; the statement-to-encoding map remains in the trusted base.

claims.claim: Four deliberately damaged controls yield SAT.
claims.scope: Confirms that removal of selected premises is observable to the encoding.

claims.claim: Exact Go big-integer arithmetic cross-checks 1,028 parameter cases.
claims.scope: Arithmetic construction, not full protocol semantics.

claims.claim: The proof route is solver-checked with an explicit trusted computing base but is not kernel-checked in Lean.
claims.scope: Submission blocker until independent review or successful mature proof-assistant build.

claims.claim: Twins uses shared-identity replicas and round-indexed communication patterns to exercise Byzantine scenarios.
claims.scope: Prior art; no novelty claim for clone/partition testing.

claims.claim: Directed per-round communication graphs and message-adversary languages predate this work.
claims.evidence: Charron-Bost & Schiper 2009; Winkler, Schmid & Moses, OPODIS 2019, DOI 10.4230/LIPIcs.OPODIS.2019.17
claims.scope: The directed-graph model is not claimed as new.

claims.claim: Communication-closure testing already gives property-preserving reductions for a suitable class of consensus implementations.
claims.scope: Current contribution is the phase-erasure safety-observation boundary, not communication closure in general.

claims.claim: Message filters, mutations, replay-capable testing, and benchmark infrastructure are existing engineering capabilities.
claims.evidence: Winter et al. 2023 DOI 10.1145/3586053; Drăgoi et al. Netrix 2024 DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-67321-4_6; Louro Neto & Ozkan 2025 DOI 10.4230/OASIcs.FMBC.2025.13
claims.scope: A richer API is explicitly excluded from the contribution.

claims.claim: No inspected source as of 17 August 2026 was found to combine phase erasure, finite agreement-observation preservation, the honest-pivot repair mechanism, and the replay boundary.
claims.scope: Absence of a found source is not proof of absolute novelty; update immediately before submission.

claims.claim: CometBFT/HotStuff terminology motivates the schema, but full production protocol-to-schema refinement is not established.
claims.scope: No production vulnerability or full conformance claim.

claims.claim: The decisive Gate 7 evidence is reproducible offline with one command and hash verification.
claims.scope: Gate 8 reproduction additionally compiles the manuscript and audits claims.

claims.claim: The legacy exact-kernel evidence is independently reproducible from the nested Gate 5 archive.
claims.scope: Gate 8 reproduction executes this route unless explicitly disabled.

claims.claim: The current working PDF has a separate cover page and an anonymous manuscript body.
claims.scope: Final LIPIcs compilation and metadata are still required.

claims.claim: Substantial language-model assistance is disclosed and human authors remain accountable.
claims.scope: Must be reviewed and retained under the final venue policy.

claims.claim: The paper does not claim a production vulnerability, universal scheduler incompleteness/minimality, liveness, prevalence, full conformance, or absolute novelty.
claims.scope: Any future edit must preserve these exclusions unless new evidence is added.

claims.claim: The manuscript is complete enough for external review but not ready for submission because proof assurance remains unresolved.
claims.scope: Submission hold is procedural and epistemic, not a claim that the theorem is false.
